claim: Hippocampome.org v1.0 established a foundational classification system identifying 122 hippocampal neuron types based on their axonal and dendritic morphologies, main neurotransmitter, membrane biophysics, and molecular expression.
source: Previously, Hippocampome.org v1.0 established a foundational classification system identifying 122 hippocampal neuron types based on their axonal and dendritic morphologies, main neurotransmitter, membrane biophysics, and molecular expression (Wheeler et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly supported by a citation to Wheeler et al., 2015, which is the original publication describing v1.0.

claim: Releases v1.1 through v1.12 increased the online information content of Hippocampome.org over 100-fold.
source: Those additional properties increased the online information content of this public resource over 100-fold, enabling numerous independent discoveries by the scientific community.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by the description of accumulated data across versions.

claim: Hippocampome.org v2.0 incorporates over 50 new neuron types.
source: Hippocampome.org v2.0, introduced here, besides incorporating over 50 new neuron types, now recenters its focus on extending the functionality to build real-scale, biologically detailed, data-driven computational simulations.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by Figure 2 showing 56 new neuron types.

claim: All freely downloadable model parameters in Hippocampome.org are directly linked to the specific peer-reviewed empirical evidence from which they were derived.
source: In all cases, the freely downloadable model parameters are directly linked to the specific peer-reviewed empirical evidence from which they were derived.
evidence: This is stated as a key feature of the resource in the abstract.

claim: Hippocampome.org can enable quantitative, multiscale analyses of circuit connectivity and spiking neural network simulations of activity dynamics.
source: Possible research applications include quantitative, multiscale analyses of circuit connectivity and spiking neural network simulations of activity dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a possible research application in the abstract.

claim: The BRAIN Initiative Cell Census Network (BICCN) was launched to establish a comprehensive reference of cell type diversity in human, mouse, and non-human primate brains.
source: The National Institutes of Health launched the BRAIN Initiative Cell Census Network (BICCN) to help establish a comprehensive reference of the cell type diversity in the human, mouse, and non-human primate brains (Hawrylycz et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hawrylycz et al., 2022.

claim: Hippocampome.org is an open-access knowledge base of the rodent hippocampal circuit at the mesoscopic level of neuron types.
source: Hippocampome.org (https://www.hippocampome.org) is an open-access knowledge base of the rodent hippocampal circuit (dentate gyrus, CA3, CA2, CA1, subiculum, and entorhinal cortex) at the mesoscopic level of neuron types (Wheeler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct description of the resource with citation support.

claim: The location of axons and dendrites across the subregions and layers of the hippocampal formation is a key property for the identification of neuron types in Hippocampome.org.
source: Specifically, a key property for the identification of neuron types in Hippocampome.org is the location of axons and dendrites across the subregions and layers of the hippocampal formation.
evidence: This is stated as a fundamental principle of the classification system.

claim: Focusing on axonal and dendritic distributions provides several considerable advantages including that these features mediate neuronal connectivity.
source: First, these features mediate neuronal connectivity, thus immediately revealing the underlying blueprint of network circuitry (Rees et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Rees et al., 2017.

claim: Axonal and dendritic distributions are widely used in the neuroscience community as a reliable and concrete anchoring signature to correlate electrophysiological and transcriptomic profiles.
source: Second, they are widely used in the neuroscience community as a reliable and concrete anchoring signature to correlate electrophysiological and transcriptomic profiles (DeFelipe et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to DeFelipe et al., 2013.

claim: Hippocampome.org v1.1 integrated a web-based interactive thesaurus mapping of synonyms and definitions to help disambiguate terminological inconsistencies in the neuroscience literature.
source: Specifically, v1.1 integrated a web-based interactive thesaurus mapping of synonyms and definitions (Hamilton et al., 2017a; hippocampome.org/find-term) to help disambiguate the many terminological inconsistencies in the neuroscience literature (Shepherd et al., 2019; Yuste et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hamilton et al., 2017a, Shepherd et al., 2019, and Yuste et al., 2020.

claim: Release v1.2 introduced the capability to browse, search, and analyze the potential connectivity between neuron types.
source: Release v1.2 introduced the capability to browse, search, and analyze the potential connectivity between neuron types (Rees et al., 2016; Hippocampome.org/connectivity) as derived from the compiled overlapping locations of all the presynaptic axons and postsynaptic dendrites.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Rees et al., 2016.

claim: Transcriptomic information was greatly expanded in v1.3, which incorporated in situ hybridization data from the Allen Brain Atlas.
source: Transcriptomic information was greatly expanded in both v1.3 (Hamilton et al., 2017b), which incorporated in situ hybridization data from the Allen Brain Atlas (Lein et al., 2007), and v1.5 (White et al., 2020), which leveraged relational inferences interlinking the region-specific expression of two or more genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hamilton et al., 2017b and Lein et al., 2007.

claim: v1.5 leveraged relational inferences interlinking the region-specific expression of two or more genes.
source: Transcriptomic information was greatly expanded in both v1.3 (Hamilton et al., 2017b), which incorporated in situ hybridization data from the Allen Brain Atlas (Lein et al., 2007), and v1.5 (White et al., 2020), which leveraged relational inferences interlinking the region-specific expression of two or more genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to White et al., 2020.

claim: The quantifications of firing pattern phenotypes in v1.6 were fitted by dynamical systems modeling in v1.7.
source: The quantifications of firing pattern phenotypes, such as rapid adapting spiking, transient stuttering, and persistent slow-wave bursting, in v1.6 (Komendantov et al., 2019; hippocampome.org/firing_patterns) were fitted by dynamical systems modeling (Izhikevich, 2003) in v1.7 (Venkadesh et al., 2019; hippocampome.org/Izhikevich).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Komendantov et al., 2019, Izhikevich, 2003, and Venkadesh et al., 2019.

claim: Release v1.9 made available measurements from in vivo recordings.
source: Although the above properties were largely measured from slice preparations, v1.9 made available measurements from in vivo recordings (Sanchez-Aguilera et al., 2021; hippocampome.org/in-vivo).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sanchez-Aguilera et al., 2021.

claim: Release v1.10 provided a compendium of cognitive functions linked to specific hippocampal neurons.
source: Release v1.10 provided a compendium of cognitive functions linked to specific hippocampal neurons (Sutton and Ascoli, 2021; hippocampome.org/cognome), while the v1.11 neuron type census estimated the population counts for each neuron type (Attili et al., 2022; hippocampome.org/census).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sutton and Ascoli, 2021.

claim: The v1.11 neuron type census estimated the population counts for each neuron type.
source: Release v1.10 provided a compendium of cognitive functions linked to specific hippocampal neurons (Sutton and Ascoli, 2021; hippocampome.org/cognome), while the v1.11 neuron type census estimated the population counts for each neuron type (Attili et al., 2022; hippocampome.org/census).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Attili et al., 2022.

claim: v1.8 calculated the synaptic probabilities and the numbers of contacts per connected pair.
source: In particular, v1.8 calculated the synaptic probabilities and the numbers of contacts per connected pair (Tecuatl et al., 2021b; hippocampome.org/syn_probabilities), and v1.4 data mined synaptic physiology (Moradi and Ascoli, 2020; hippocampome.org/synaptome), with conductance, time constant, and short-term plasticity values normalized by age, temperature, species, sex, and recording method in v1.12 (Moradi et al., 2022; hippocampome.org/synapse), leveraging machine learning and a phenomenological model (Tsodyks et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Tecuatl et al., 2021b.

claim: v1.4 data mined synaptic physiology.
source: In particular, v1.8 calculated the synaptic probabilities and the numbers of contacts per connected pair (Tecuatl et al., 2021b; hippocampome.org/syn_probabilities), and v1.4 data mined synaptic physiology (Moradi and Ascoli, 2020; hippocampome.org/synaptome), with conductance, time constant, and short-term plasticity values normalized by age, temperature, species, sex, and recording method in v1.12 (Moradi et al., 2022; hippocampome.org/synapse), leveraging machine learning and a phenomenological model (Tsodyks et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Moradi and Ascoli, 2020.

claim: v1.12 normalized conductance, time constant, and short-term plasticity values by age, temperature, species, sex, and recording method, leveraging machine learning and a phenomenological model.
source: In particular, v1.8 calculated the synaptic probabilities and the numbers of contacts per connected pair (Tecuatl et al., 2021b; hippocampome.org/syn_probabilities), and v1.4 data mined synaptic physiology (Moradi and Ascoli, 2020; hippocampome.org/synaptome), with conductance, time constant, and short-term plasticity values normalized by age, temperature, species, sex, and recording method in v1.12 (Moradi et al., 2022; hippocampome.org/synapse), leveraging machine learning and a phenomenological model (Tsodyks et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Moradi et al., 2022 and Tsodyks et al., 1998.

claim: Hippocampome.org v2.0 expanded the catalog with 56 new neuron types across 5 of the 6 subregions of the hippocampal formation.
source: Comprehensive literature mining following the same process expanded the Hippocampome.org v2.0 catalog with 56 new neuron types across 5 of the 6 subregions of the hippocampal formation (Figure 2), including axonal-dendritic morphological patterns (Figure 2A), molecular expression (Figure 2B), and membrane biophysics (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Converging evidence indicates that Entorhinal Cortex Layer III Pyramidal cells have axonal projections in all layers of CA1.
source: For instance, converging evidence indicates that Entorhinal Cortex Layer III Pyramidal cells have axonal projections in all layers of CA1 (Deller et al., 1996; Takács et al., 2012), not just in stratum lacunosum-moleculare (SLM) as originally reported (Steward, 1976).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Deller et al., 1996 and Takács et al., 2012.

claim: The annotation of neuron type-specific firing phases relative to in vivo oscillations in v1.9 highlighted a clear distinction between Superficial and Deep CA1 Pyramidal cells.
source: The annotation of neuron type-specific firing phases relative to in vivo oscillations in v1.9 highlighted a clear distinction between Superficial and Deep CA1 Pyramidal cells (Sanchez-Aguilera et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sanchez-Aguilera et al., 2021.

claim: CA2 projects preferentially to the deep sublayer of CA1.
source: (B3) CA2 projects preferentially to the deep sublayer of CA1 (Kohara et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kohara et al., 2014.

claim: More perisomatic parvalbumin-positive GABAergic boutons are found at CA1 Deep Pyramidal cells.
source: More perisomatic parvalbumin-positive (PV+) GABAergic boutons are found at CA1 Deep Pyramidal cells (Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Valero et al., 2015.

claim: CA1 Superficial Pyramidal cells form more frequent connections to PV+ CA1 Basket cells.
source: CA1 Superficial Pyramidal cells form more frequent connections to PV + CA1 Basket cells, and PV + CA1 Basket cells form significantly more perisomatic axon terminals on CA1 Deep Pyramidal cells (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2014.

claim: PV+ CA1 Basket cells form significantly more perisomatic axon terminals on CA1 Deep Pyramidal cells.
source: CA1 Superficial Pyramidal cells form more frequent connections to PV + CA1 Basket cells, and PV + CA1 Basket cells form significantly more perisomatic axon terminals on CA1 Deep Pyramidal cells (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2014.

claim: At the time of this writing, Hippocampome.org has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits.
source: To date, the site has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits, and the original publication has been cited more than hundred times.
evidence: This is a direct statement of usage statistics.

claim: The original Hippocampome.org publication has been cited more than hundred times.
source: To date, the site has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits, and the original publication has been cited more than hundred times.
evidence: This is a direct statement of citation statistics.

claim: An early application of Hippocampome.org-sourced data used subthreshold biophysical measures for multicompartmental models of signal integration and extracellular field generation.
source: An early application of Hippocampome.org-sourced data used subthreshold biophysical measures, such as input resistance and membrane time constant, for multicompartmental models of signal integration and extracellular field generation (Gulyás et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gulyás et al., 2016.

claim: Gulyás et al., 2016 concluded that somatic and proximal dendritic intracellular recordings in pyramidal cells and calretinin-positive interneurons do not capture a sizable portion of the synaptic inputs.
source: That study concluded that somatic and proximal dendritic intracellular recordings in pyramidal cells and calretinin-positive interneurons, in particular, do not capture a sizable portion of the synaptic inputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cited study by Gulyás et al., 2016.

claim: Schumm et al., 2022 employed Hippocampome.org as the primary information resource for neuron types in DG, CA3, and CA1.
source: As a recent usage example, another lab employed Hippocampome.org as the primary information resource for neuron types in DG, CA3, and CA1 (Schumm et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schumm et al., 2022.

claim: Schumm et al., 2022 discovered that mild traumatic brain injury may affect the broadband power in CA3 and CA1 and the phase coherence between CA3 and CA1.
source: They discovered that mild traumatic brain injury, in the form of alterations in spike-timing-dependent plasticity, may affect the broadband power in CA3 and CA1 and the phase coherence between CA3 and CA1.
evidence: This is a finding from the cited study by Schumm et al., 2022.

claim: Building a data-driven circuit model of a neural system requires four essential quantities: the number of neurons in each type, the input-output response function for each neuron type, the connection probability for each pair of interacting neuron types, and the unitary synaptic signals for each pair of connected neuron types.
source: Specifically, building a data-driven circuit model of a neural system (such as the hippocampal formation or portion thereof) requires four essential quantities besides the full list of neuron types (Bahmer et al., 2023; DePasquale et al., 2023): (i) the number of neurons in each type; (ii) the input-output response function for each neuron type; (iii) the connection probability for each pair of interacting neuron types; and (iv) the unitary synaptic signals for each pair of connected neuron types (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bahmer et al., 2023 and DePasquale et al., 2023, and illustrated in Figure 5.

claim: Hippocampome.org v1.11 provides estimates of the number of neurons in each neuron type for both rats and mice.
source: Hippocampome.org v1.11 provides estimates of the number of neurons in each neuron type (i) for both rats and mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: The neuron type census values in v1.11 were derived in a two-step process: first, literature mining extracted suitable quantitative relations; second, numerical optimization of the corresponding equations yielded a complete census for all neuron types.
source: These values were derived in a two-step process (Attili et al., 2020): first, literature mining extracted suitable quantitative relations such as the cellular density in a given layer (Attili et al., 2019), the total count of neurons expressing a certain gene, or the fraction of sampled cells with a particular morphology; second, numerical optimization of the corresponding equations yielded a complete census for all neuron types.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Attili et al., 2020 and Attili et al., 2019.

claim: As of v1.7, Hippocampome.org represents the neuronal input-output response function in the form of single- and multi-compartment Izhikevich models fitted by evolutionary algorithms.
source: As of v1.7, Hippocampome.org represents the neuronal input-output response function (ii) in the form of single- and multi-compartment Izhikevich models (Figure 5B) fitted by evolutionary algorithms to accurately reproduce the observed firing behavior of each neuron type (Venkadesh et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Venkadesh et al., 2018 and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: For v1.8, the connection probability from one neuron type to another was computed from measurements of the appropriate axonal and dendritic lengths in each invaded subregion and layer.
source: For v1.8, the connection probability (iii) from one neuron type to another (Figure 5C) was computed from measurements of the appropriate axonal and dendritic lengths in each invaded subregion and layer (hippocampome.org/A-D_lengths).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 5C.

claim: Hippocampome.org v1.12 adopted the Tsodyks-Pawelzik-Markram formulation, representing unitary signals and short-term plasticity with five constants for each directional pair of interacting neuron types.
source: As for the synaptic communication between neurons (iv), Hippocampome.org v1.12 adopted the Tsodyks-Pawelzik-Markram formulation, representing unitary signals and short-term plasticity with five constants for each directional pair of interacting neuron types: the synaptic conductance, decay time, recovery time, facilitation time, and the utilization ratio (Tsodyks et al., 1998; Moradi et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tsodyks et al., 1998 and Moradi et al., 2022.

claim: The synaptic parameters in v1.12 were fitted from experimental data employing deep learning to account for numerous experimental variables including species, sex, age, recording temperature, and clamping configuration.
source: Once again, these parameters were fitted from the experimental data (Cutsuridis et al., 2018) employing deep learning to account for (and predict the effects of) numerous experimental variables (Figure 5D), including species (rat vs. mouse), sex (male vs. female), age (young vs. adult), recording temperature (room vs. body), and clamping configuration (voltage vs. current).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cutsuridis et al., 2018 and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Each neuron page in Hippocampome.org links out to all three-dimensional morphological reconstructions of the same cell type available in NeuroMorpho.Org.
source: For example, each neuron page links out to all three-dimensional morphological reconstructions of the same cell type available in NeuroMorpho.Org (Ascoli et al., 2007), and selected data from NeuroMorpho.Org were used to compute axonal and dendritic length and connection probabilities.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ascoli et al., 2007.

claim: Selected data from NeuroMorpho.Org were used to compute axonal and dendritic length and connection probabilities in Hippocampome.org.
source: For example, each neuron page links out to all three-dimensional morphological reconstructions of the same cell type available in NeuroMorpho.Org (Ascoli et al., 2007), and selected data from NeuroMorpho.Org were used to compute axonal and dendritic length and connection probabilities.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the integration with NeuroMorpho.Org.

claim: Each neuron page in Hippocampome.org links out to all computational models involving the same cell type on ModelDB.
source: Each neuron page also links out to all computational models (including Hodgkin-Huxley, stochastic diffusion, mean firing rate, etc.) involving the same cell type on ModelDB (McDougal et al., 2017), while conversely ModelDB includes the Izhikevich models for all Hippocampome.org neuron types.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to McDougal et al., 2017.

claim: ModelDB includes the Izhikevich models for all Hippocampome.org neuron types.
source: Each neuron page also links out to all computational models (including Hodgkin-Huxley, stochastic diffusion, mean firing rate, etc.) involving the same cell type on ModelDB (McDougal et al., 2017), while conversely ModelDB includes the Izhikevich models for all Hippocampome.org neuron types.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the integration with ModelDB.

claim: Simulation parameters from Hippocampome.org are exportable to the CARLsim simulation environment.
source: Moreover, simulation parameters from Hippocampome.org are exportable to the CARLsim simulation environment (Nageswaran et al., 2009), enabling fast execution of spiking neural network models optimized for GPUs.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Nageswaran et al., 2009.

claim: Hippocampome.org harnessed data from the Allen Brain Atlas to infer gene expression for principal neurons and cell densities for use in the neuron type census.
source: Furthermore, Hippocampome.org harnessed data from the Allen Brain Atlas (Lein et al., 2007) to infer gene expression for principal neurons and cell densities for use in the neuron type census.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lein et al., 2007.

claim: Hippocampome.org v2.0 includes a new graphical user interface that allows users to download sets of simulation parameter values for arbitrarily selected neuron types, a subregion of interest, or the whole hippocampal formation.
source: To facilitate construction of spiking neural network simulations, Hippocampome.org v2.0 also includes a new graphical user interface (GUI). With this GUI, users can download sets of simulation parameter values for arbitrarily selected neuron types, a subregion of interest, or the whole hippocampal formation (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Hippocampome.org informally ranks the importance of each neuron type in terms of the functional role it plays in the hippocampal circuitry from 1 (essential) to 5 (dispensable).
source: For the convenience of users interested in simplified circuit models, Hippocampome.org informally ranks the importance of each neuron type in terms of the functional role it plays in the hippocampal circuitry from 1 (essential) to 5 (dispensable).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the ranking system.

claim: When Hippocampome.org is missing a parameter value due to insufficient experimental evidence, the GUI exports a default value clearly indicating so in the downloadable files.
source: When Hippocampome.org is missing a parameter value due to insufficient experimental evidence, the GUI exports a default value clearly indicating so in the downloadable files.
evidence: This is a direct statement of how missing data are handled.

claim: For missing synaptic probabilities, Hippocampome.org precomputes values averaged by connection type: excitatory-excitatory (0.0117), excitatory-inhibitory (0.0237), inhibitory-excitatory (0.00684), and inhibitory-inhibitory (0.00423).
source: For missing synaptic probabilities, Hippocampome.org precomputes values averaged by connection type, namely excitatory-excitatory (0.0117), excitatory-inhibitory (0.0237), inhibitory-excitatory (0.00684), and inhibitory-inhibitory (0.00423).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the default values used for missing data.

claim: An ongoing line of research focuses on a real-scale mouse model of CA3 investigating the cellular mechanisms of pattern completion.
source: An ongoing line of research in this regard focuses on a real-scale mouse model of CA3, with the eventual goal of investigating the cellular mechanisms of pattern completion.
evidence: This is a direct statement of ongoing research.

claim: Initial work on the CA3 model included excitatory Pyramidal cells and seven main inhibitory interneuron types: Axo-axonic cells, Basket cells, Basket Cholecystokinin-positive cells, Bistratified cells, Ivy cells, Mossy Fiber-Associated ORDEN cells, and QuadD-LM cells.
source: Initial work included excitatory Pyramidal cells and seven main inhibitory interneuron types: Axo-axonic cells (AAC), Basket cells (BC), Basket Cholecystokinin-positive cells (BC CCK+), Bistratified cells (BiC), Ivy cells, Mossy Fiber-Associated ORDEN (MFA ORDEN) cells, and QuadD-LM (QuadD) cells (Kopsick et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kopsick et al., 2023.

claim: Use of Hippocampome.org parameters for cell census, Izhikevich models, synaptic signals, and connection probabilities resulted in robust, realistic, rhythmic resting state activity for all neuron types in the CA3 model.
source: Use of Hippocampome.org parameters for cell census, Izhikevich models, synaptic signals, and connection probabilities resulted in robust, realistic, rhythmic resting state activity for all neuron types (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 9A.

claim: Another pursuit using a spiking neural network seeks to replicate the spatial representation in grid cells, modeled utilizing Hippocampome.org Medial Entorhinal Cortex Layer II Stellate cells.
source: Another pursuit using a spiking neural network seeks to replicate the spatial representation in grid cells (Sargolini et al., 2006), modeled utilizing Hippocampome.org Medial Entorhinal Cortex Layer II Stellate cells (SC), and supported by various GABAergic interneuron types (Dhillon and Jones, 2000): Axo-axonic (AA), Basket cells (BC), and Entorhinal Cortex Layer II Basket-Multipolar cells (BC MP).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sargolini et al., 2006 and Dhillon and Jones, 2000.

claim: A spiking neural network implementation of the continuous attractor model generates grid field activity highly compatible with that measured in behaving animals when utilizing Hippocampome.org model parameters.
source: Our work, which is in preparation for publication, demonstrates that a spiking neural network implementation of one such theory, the continuous attractor model, generates grid field activity highly compatible with that measured in behaving animals when utilizing Hippocampome.org model parameters.
evidence: This is a statement of preliminary research findings.

claim: Hippocampome.org has established itself prominently amongst other readily accessible, evidence-based, expert-curated bioscience public resources such as FlyBase, WormBase, the Blue Brain Project, SynGO, and RegenBase.
source: Hippocampome.org, through its continuous updates and conspicuous usage, has established itself prominently amongst other readily accessible, evidence-based, expert-curated bioscience public resources of note, such as FlyBase for Drosophila molecular biology (The FlyBase Consortium, 1994; dos Santos et al., 2015), WormBase for nematode genomics (Stein et al., 2001), the Blue Brain Project for somatosensory cortex (Markram, 2006), SynGO for synaptic functions (Koopmans et al., 2019), and RegenBase for spinal cord injury biology (Callahan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple comparable resources.

claim: Hippocampome.org has evolved from being a storehouse of information in v1.0–1.12 to a platform in v2.0 for launching detailed simulations of the hippocampal formation.
source: Hippocampome.org has evolved from being a storehouse of information in v1.0–1.12, along the lines of FlyBase, WormBase, SynGO, and RegenBase, to a platform in v2.0 for launching detailed simulations of the hippocampal formation, in the vein of the Blue Brain Project.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the evolution of the resource.

claim: Hippocampome.org distinguishes itself in its reliance wholly on already published data and the more tailored focus on a single portion of the brain.
source: However, Hippocampome.org distinguishes itself in its reliance wholly on already published data and the more tailored focus on a single portion of the brain.
evidence: This is a direct statement of distinguishing features.

claim: The foundation for Hippocampome.org has always been the data that are published in the literature.
source: The foundation for Hippocampome.org has always been the data that are published in the literature.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the foundational principle.

claim: Some of the simulation-ready parameters in Hippocampome.org are the result of modeling, such as the neuronal input/output functions (Izhikevich model) and the unitary synaptic values (Tsodyks-Pawelzik-Markram model).
source: Nevertheless, some of the simulation-ready parameters now also included in Hippocampome.org are indeed the result of modeling, such as the neuronal input/output functions (Izhikevich model; Izhikevich, 2003) and the unitary synaptic values (Tsodyks-Pawelzik-Markram model; Tsodyks et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Izhikevich, 2003 and Tsodyks et al., 1998.

claim: Other simulation-ready parameters in Hippocampome.org are the result of specific analysis approaches, including the connection probabilities (axonal-dendritic spatial overlaps) and the neuron type census (numerical optimization of all constraints).
source: Other simulation-ready parameters are the result of specific analysis approaches, including the connection probabilities (axonal-dendritic spatial overlaps) and the neuron type census (numerical optimization of all constraints).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the analysis approaches used.

claim: To date, the Hippocampome.org site has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits.
source: To date, the site has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits, and the original publication has been cited more than hundred times.
evidence: This is a direct statement of usage statistics.

claim: The original Hippocampome.org publication has been cited more than hundred times.
source: To date, the site has been visited over 136,000 times with over 33,000 unique visits, and the original publication has been cited more than hundred times.
evidence: This is a direct statement of citation statistics.

claim: The focus of Hippocampome.org will shift from development to exploitation through the in silico emulation of complex dynamics observed in vivo and in vitro.
source: Gradually, the focus of this resource will shift from development to exploitation through the in silico emulation of complex dynamics observed in vivo and in vitro, with the goal of shedding light on the underlying synaptic-level computational mechanisms.
evidence: This is a statement of future direction.

claim: The creation of real-scale spiking neural network models of the hippocampal formation and its subregions can foster biologically realistic, data-driven, mesoscopic simulations of cognitive function and dysfunction.
source: The creation of real-scale spiking neural network models of the hippocampal formation and its subregions can foster biologically realistic, data-driven, mesoscopic simulations of cognitive function and dysfunction (Sutton and Ascoli, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sutton and Ascoli, 2021.

claim: Simulations with Hippocampome.org's real-scale model of the dentate gyrus can build on previous network models of epileptogenesis by providing further clarity to the roles of all documented neuron types and their corresponding potential connections in seizure initiation and propagation.
source: For instance, simulations with Hippocampome.org's real-scale model of the dentate gyrus can build on previous network models of epileptogenesis (Dyhrfjeld-Johnsen et al., 2007) by providing further clarity to the roles of all documented neuron types and their corresponding potential connections in seizure initiation and propagation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Dyhrfjeld-Johnsen et al., 2007.

claim: A real-scale model of CA1 can aim to further the insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the circuit during theta oscillations.
source: A real-scale model of CA1 can aim to further the insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the circuit during theta oscillations (Bezaire et al., 2016; Navas-Olive et al., 2020; Romani et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bezaire et al., 2016, Navas-Olive et al., 2020, and Romani et al., 2023.

claim: Network models involving multiple subregions can open new vistas on unexplored territories, such as the use of real-scale models of the entorhinal cortex and CA2 to simulate the neuron- and connection-type specific mechanisms of social memory.
source: Furthermore, network models involving multiple subregions can open new vistas on unexplored territories, such as the use of real-scale models of the entorhinal cortex and CA2 to simulate the neuron- and connection-type specific mechanisms of social memory (Lopez-Rojas et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lopez-Rojas et al., 2022.

claim: To compute estimates of connection probabilities and numbers of contacts per connected pair for the rat mossy fiber-CA3 circuit, the study used previously calculated average convex hull volume and several measurements from Acsády et al., 1998.
source: To compute estimates of connection probabilities and numbers of contacts per connected pair for the rat mossy fiber-CA3 circuit, we used previously calculated average convex hull volume (Tecuatl et al., 2021b) and several measurements from a seminal anatomical study (Acsády et al., 1998): DG Granule cell axonal length within CA3 (3,236 µm), inter-bouton distances for mossy boutons on Pyramidal cell targets in CA3c (162 µm) and in the rest of CA3 (284 µm), and inter-bouton distances for en-passant and filipodia boutons onto CA3 interneurons (67.4 µm, considering that 48 interneurons can be contacted by a single GC).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tecuatl et al., 2021b and Acsády et al., 1998.

claim: The calculations for the mossy fiber-CA3 circuit assume that DG Granule cells only innervate CA3 stratum lucidum.
source: Given that the mossy fibers innervate mainly CA3 SL, and due to the lack of information regarding the exact proportion of axons innervating CA3 SP, these calculations assume that GCs only innervate SL.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an assumption in the calculations.

claim: To compute estimates of connection probabilities and numbers of contacts per connected pair for the rat Schaffer collaterals-CA1 circuit, the study utilized previously reported values for the distinct axonal innervation patterns in CA1 from CA3 Pyramidal cells and CA3c Pyramidal cells.
source: To compute estimates of connection probabilities and numbers of contacts per connected pair for the rat Schaffer collaterals-CA1 circuit, we utilized previously reported values for the distinct axonal innervation patterns (Ropireddy et al., 2011; Sik et al., 1993; Wittner et al., 2007) in CA1 stratum radiatum (SR) and stratum oriens (SO) from CA3 Pyramidal cells (27.5% of total axonal length: 64% to SR, 15% to stratum pyramidale (SP), 21% to SO) and CA3c Pyramidal cells (64.1% of total axonal length: 94% to SR, 3% to SP, 3% to SO).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ropireddy et al., 2011, Sik et al., 1993, and Wittner et al., 2007.

claim: The study used the average inter-bouton distance reported for the Schaffer collaterals in stratum radiatum (4.47 µm) and stratum oriens (5.8 µm).

evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 1994.
